public_rationale: Both parts of the sentence are hedged. Neither lab 'appears' unable to serve customers, and neither 'appears' to improve its products based on compute. The sentence sits inside a rhetorical question about why data centers are needed. The speaker sets no test for what counts as being unable to serve customers or as improving products because of compute, and he exempts Claude's uptime. As context, The Register reported that on 2026-03-25 Anthropic adjusted Claude's peak-hour session limits to balance demand with its capacity (e1). Whether a change like this counts against the claim depends on a test the speaker did not give. Scoring the claim would mean turning a stated impression into a firm claim and choosing an unstated test, so it is not scored.
limitations: This judgement covers only the hedged sentence as written. A firmer version could be tested against company statements on compute constraints.
The packet contains one context report on Anthropic and none on OpenAI.

our_interpretation: Both parts are hedged with 'appears' and sit inside a rhetorical question ('why do we need these fucking things?'). They give the speaker's impression, not a firm factual assertion.

The speaker sets no measure for 'unable to serve customers' or 'improve their products based on the availability of compute', and he exempts Claude's uptime problems. Any test, such as treating usage limits as a failure to serve or limit increases as compute-driven improvement, would be the evaluator's own reading.
Under these rules, plain readings apply only to firm claims, so this one is not scored.
criteria.support_condition: Not scored. A firm version would be supported by evidence that neither lab turned away customers or delayed or limited products because of compute shortages, and that new compute did not lead to product changes.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Not scored. A firm version would be contradicted by statements from OpenAI or Anthropic tying service limits or product improvements to compute availability, beyond Claude's uptime.
